cr_data.provenance:
The artist, New York, then Abiquiu, N. Mex.; Downtown Gallery (Edith Halpert, dealer), New York, by February 1953 [see note 1]; transferred to Doris Bry (1920–2014, dealer), New York, about 1963 [see note 2]; sold through Doris Bry (1920–2014, dealer), New York, to Donald Clifford Gallup (1913–2000), New Haven, Conn., 1967 [see note 3];  bequeathed to the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University, New Haven, Conn., 2001; transferred to the Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven, Conn., 2019 
Note 1: In 1953, the painting was on loan from the Downtown Gallery to the Dallas Museum of Art. The Downtown Gallery had exclusive representation of the artist between 1950–1963. 
Note 2: Doris Bry took over exclusive representation of the artist from Downtown Gallery by 1963. (Jo Ann Lewis, “Doris Bry The Legend of O’Keeffe,” Washington Post, January 7, 1990; “Timeline,” https://www.okeeffemuseum.org/timeline/, accessed September 29, 2025). 
Note 3: Correspondence between Gallup, the artist and Bry, indicates that the painting was sold to Gallup through Bry on behalf of the artist (Gallup correspondence, November 3, 1966–February 18, 1969, Donald Clifford Gallup Papers, Beinecke Rare Books and Manuscripts Library, YCAL MSS 838, accession 14, Box 50, copies in accession file) 
(Source: Yale University Art Gallery, 2025)

description: A low, reddish-brown adobe house with white-trimmed windows stretches across the composition. The house stands on an expanse of green earth, and the blue form of Pedernal rises in the distance behind it. A blue sky with a few wispy clouds fills the top of the image.
title: The House I Live In
